primary_antecedent.receiving_contribution: Independent full geometric proof with changing-symbol glancing compactness, stationary states, normalized travel-time bounds and a nested-exhaustion argument that does not assume first-exit continuity.

source_correspondence: S0 quantifies over every maximal generalized continuation through the target, including stationary normalized rays and nonunique infinite-contact continuations. It proves compact access and a finite normalized travel-time bound uniformly for small parameters.

S1 derives every projected Hamilton equation, including the actual normalization term h v. Boundary-normal coordinates and their inverses vary smoothly with the parameter. A negative principal normalization reverses local orientation; that sign is retained when returning to the global parameter.

S2 constructs a reflection-invariant positive homogeneous scale, with uniform compact bounds on changes of time. Compressed coordinates and squared normal momentum remain uniformly Lipschitz across accumulating reflections, and the absolute normal momentum has a uniform one-half Holder modulus.

S3 uses a dense-time diagonal and finite grids to obtain uniform compressed convergence while the principal symbol changes. S4 passes the actual integral equations in the interior and the simple hitting equation at a transverse reflection.

S5 retains a positive normal acceleration at strict diffraction, proves at most one reflection and a vanishing limiting jump, and recovers the ordinary tangent trajectory. The strict-gliding energy derivative contains the normalization term and controls arbitrarily many reflections.

S6 retains the extra nonnegative diagonal normalization coefficient in the cooperative comparison. Shortest matrix paths give the exact forcing moments, and at higher contact give x=O(t^3), absolute v=O(t^2), tangential error O(t^4). The limiting derivative law does not require infinite-contact uniqueness.

Stationary gliding and radial projected states are included. S7 combines actual local existence, finite-endpoint joining and a compact buffer to give uniform local lifetime. Only finite endpoints must escape compact subsets.

S8 takes subsequential limits of nested exit-interval endpoints and curves, without assuming first-exit continuity. S9 proves that the limit avoids the entire open observation region. S10 uses uniform buffers to rule out extendible finite endpoints and obtains the maximal limiting ray that contradicts the access hypothesis.

S11 records the exact quantifiers: constants depend on the compact target and the qualitative global access hypothesis. The proof supplies geometric stability, not the still-required uniform analytic estimate.

Three complete solutions verify an exact quadratic reflected family with unbounded reflection count, a stationary limiting operator whose observation times diverge, and a smooth family of paths with discontinuous first-exit times. The reproducible figure uses exact quadratic Bezier arcs for the normal excursions, with all other phase coordinates explicitly given in the lesson.

Forty-one exact checks, 240 parsed formulas, 26 displays and fourteen inspected lesson captures support the receiving review. Finite checks are not evidence by themselves for the analytic compactness or existence arguments.
